title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is seeing a mix of new partnerships and funding initiatives aimed at enhancing military capabilities and data infrastructure. Meanwhile, the ongoing challenges in hypersonic testing and geopolitical tensions continue to shape the landscape.

themes.title: New Players in Space Supply
themes.body: The Commercial Space Federation's latest members signal a growing interest in the space supply chain. This trend could lead to increased competition and innovation in logistics and support for space missions.

themes.title: Military Space Mobility Gains Ground
themes.body: UK startup Applied Atomics is making its move into the US market, focusing on military space mobility. This could be a sign of increasing transatlantic collaboration in defense technologies.

themes.title: Funding Boosts Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup adds $1.4 billion for space resilience, reflecting a serious commitment to fortifying space capabilities. This funding could enhance both defensive and operational readiness in an increasingly contested domain.

themes.title: Hypersonic Testing Woes Continue
themes.body: The latest hypersonic glide-vehicle test has slipped again, marking the third consecutive quarter of delays. This raises questions about the current state of US capabilities in this critical area of defense technology.
